tips.title: Aligning Wings with a Jig - Trumpeter Example
tips.text: For Trumpeter's 1/48 F-16, create a wing alignment jig using a scrap of wood and a drill bit matching the wing's mounting peg. Insert the peg into the jig, apply Tamiya Extra Thin Cement along the wing root's edge, then gently press the wing onto the fuselage. Hold it in place for 30 seconds. Remove the jig, let it cure for 30 minutes.

tips.title: Installing Photo-Etch Parts - Eduard PE Set
tips.text: Before installing Eduard PE parts, soak them in warm water for a few minutes. This makes bending easier. Use Eduard's 'Super Glue' for attachment. Apply a small dot on the part, wait 10 seconds, then attach it to the model. For intricate parts, use tweezers and a hobby knife to trim excess.

tips.title: Working with Resin Conversion Kits - Clear Prop Models
tips.text: Resin parts are delicate. Before assembly, test fit all pieces. Use super glue for joins, applying it sparingly. For strength, insert a thin brass rod (0.5mm) into drilled holes. After assembly, use Vallejo Plastic Putty to fill seams, let dry, then sand smooth.

tips.title: Assembling Tracks - Arma Hobby Individual Links
tips.text: Arma Hobby's individual link tracks require careful handling. Dry fit all links, then apply Tamiya Extra Thin Cement to each joint. Allow 30 seconds for the cement to become tacky. Press the links together, maintaining the correct track width. Once assembled, attach the track runs to the model's road wheels.

tips.title: Strengthening Thin Parts with Brass Rod - Meng Tanks
tips.text: Meng's tanks often have thin, fragile parts. Strengthen them by drilling small holes and inserting brass rod (0.5mm or 1mm). Cut the rod to length, apply super glue to both the rod and the drilled hole, then insert. Clamp the part gently until the glue sets. Sand any excess rod flush with the surface.
